A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OF-Diff. All 13 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v3, including supplementary material, are readable. Equations, tables, figures, and relocated content support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original DIOR/DOTA generation, downstream detection, unseen-layout, and ablation results, including supplementary per-class results.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds original HRSC2016 results, robustness and sensitivity analyses, computational measurements, and human/GPT assessments.

M1.justification: ESGM, the shape/mix branches, stop-gradient teaching, and KNN/KL-based DDPO are retained. Online distillation reframes the existing consistency mechanism. The corrected Eq. 6 matches v1's prose and Figure 3, while the stated consistency weight of 1 preserves the original weighting; an underlying procedure change is not established.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained DIOR-R and DOTA coverage, v3 evaluates HRSC2016 using 26 ship categories and explicitly examines heavily occluded objects. Appendix A.6 also introduces human/GPT evaluation of realism and aesthetics, substantially extending the represented cases and evaluation tasks.

E2.justification: LayoutDiffusion, GLIGEN, AeroGen, and CC-Diff remain the comparison methods in corresponding benchmark and unseen-layout experiments. The same set is used for the new HRSC2016 and cost comparisons. The real-only downstream baseline is retained in the relocated trainability table.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include a consistency-weight sweep, seven real/generated-data compositions, training with versus without heavily occluded samples, and computational-cost measurements. The questionnaire uses 20 randomly ordered image pairs and 16 human participants. Unseen-layout evaluation adds mAP and mAP75. Existing DIOR/DOTA splits, preprocessing, and training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: The component ablation expands from six combinations to all eight and adds generation-fidelity metrics. v3 also adds consistency-weight sensitivity, occlusion/mask-failure cases, synthetic-data scaling, computational-cost analysis, and quantitative human/GPT and feature-space examinations of the caption tradeoff. Existing unseen-layout and diversity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix A.6 newly reports three GPT-5 evaluation rounds and averages selection counts across human annotators or repeated GPT evaluations. This adds repeated-evaluation and aggregation information. Neither version reports seed-based variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the benchmark results.

E6.justification: Matched DIOR/DOTA benchmark, shape-fidelity, downstream, and per-class scores are unchanged. Substantial new results include HRSC2016 FID 77.91 and mAP50 64.1, versus CC-Diff's 84.55 and 62.57 in Table 5; occlusion FIDs of 79.26 versus 77.91 in Figure 7; and data-mixture, cost, preference, sensitivity, and expanded ablation results. Table 3 also adds unseen-layout mAP/mAP75 entries.

T1.justification: Eq. 6 corrects the printed consistency-loss student term from the mixed prediction to the shape prediction, resolving its mismatch with v1's explanation. The DDPO Markov-decision-process equations are retained in Appendix A.1. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: v3 removes the abstract's explicit claim to be first to extract layout-based shape priors for remote-sensing diffusion. Otherwise, the central claims about reference-free sampling, object fidelity, difficult-object generation, and downstream benefits remain, with the dual-branch mechanism now presented as online distillation.

C2.justification: v1 primarily warns that distorted masks impair generation. v3 qualifies this by arguing that complete mask failures are rare and observed occlusion-related anomalies have little aggregate impact. It also adds applicability conclusions about synthetic-only training, diminishing returns from additional synthetic data, computational practicality, and selecting more suitable mask extractors.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies consistency weight 1, KNN k=50, KL weight 2, feature-based reward calculations, questionnaire prompts, and resource-use measurements, and updates the repository pointer. v1's explicit four-H100 training-hardware statement is removed. The new reward details remain inconsistent: Section 3.4 specifies CLIP features, whereas Appendix A.1 specifies ResNet101.

R1.justification: v3 adds the HRSC2016 dataset citation, Liu et al. (2017), and removes the explicit first-use novelty claim from the abstract. The related-work coverage and positioning against existing generation methods otherwise remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and central architecture explanation are substantially rewritten around online distillation. The document introduces numbered sections and a structured seven-part appendix, relocating DDPO formalization and portions of the discussion and experimental presentation. Terminology changes throughout, although much related-work and results prose is retained.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the two-column format with a single-column design and redesigned title page. Figure 1 is redrawn, ESGM is incorporated into Figure 3, the qualitative comparison grid changes, and sensitivity plots accompany the per-class charts. Tables are reorganized and expanded, with new appendix displays and relocation of existing results and illustrations.

improvement.justification: The added HRSC2016 validation, fuller ablations, practical stress tests, and direct caption-preference assessments strengthen empirical support, while Eq. 6 resolves an existing formula inconsistency. These gains are tempered by reporting problems: CLIP versus ResNet101 reward features remain contradictory, and Appendix A.6 claims a 1.15-point caption-related reduction although Figure 9 shows 1.47 versus 0.52, a 0.95-point difference. Overall support and clarity improve, but reproducibility and numerical consistency remain imperfect.
